purpose: Verify that two individually valid editorial sidecars with incompatible claims produce CONFLICT while preserving both histories and selecting neither.

activities.label: validate two sidecars independently and compare claims within the same asset timeline and version scope
attack candidate count identity hash version permissions events and silent selection
record preserved histories and remaining authority resolution unknowns

queries.expression: can two individually valid sidecars with the same asset hash version and timeline be distinguished as incompatible claims
does the result preserve every candidate and refuse silent last-write-wins selection
do incomplete or unsafe candidates produce BLOCKED rather than a conflict or compatible composition
does conflict auditing reuse the 074 sidecar validator and shared event replay without a new core

assumptions: Both sidecars are synthetic and individually consistent with the declared source registry.
The common asset hash version and timeline identify the scope in which claims are compared.
Different marker references or source frames are semantically incompatible claims for this audit.
A conflict has no valid automatic winner without an authority and resolution policy.
Preserving both histories is safer than overwriting one candidate.
kill_tests: Missing candidate blocks the conflict audit.
Duplicate sidecar identity blocks the conflict audit.
Cross-asset identity blocks the conflict audit.
Stale hash blocks the conflict audit.
Stale version blocks the conflict audit.
Writable sidecar blocks the conflict audit.
Non-dry-run action blocks the conflict audit.
Preferred sidecar selection blocks the conflict audit.
Missing required event blocks the conflict audit.
Identical claims cannot be labeled as a conflict.
unknowns: Which institutional authority can resolve a conflict between valid sidecars.
Whether signatures, publication time or vector versions are required for real sidecars.
How file replacement and concurrent editors should be represented.
Whether semantic equivalence needs a richer claim normalization than this marker-focused fixture.
Whether a real editorial system can expose the required provenance without privileged access.
